examples.problem:
Let $F(x)=-6x-2$ for $x\in[0,\pi).$ Find the missing parts in the Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function $F(x).$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068558/assets/ee53aca390d2803fa92f3239dc7548792c6be9e4c05a102fe936aeb9e7ced6d6.png)
examples.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
a_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi f(x)\cos(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-6x-2$ for $x \in (0,\pi).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
a_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi (-6x-2) \cos(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=-6x-2\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=-6 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =\frac{2}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{1}{n}[(-6x-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{6}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{2}{n\pi }(((-6\pi -2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))-\frac{6}{n}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{2}{n\pi }(0-\frac{6}{n}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{12(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi ))}{{n}^{2}\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $\cos(n\pi)=(-1)^n,$ we have

$$
a_n = \dfrac{12(1-(-1)^n)}{\pi n^2}.
$$

Finally, the Fourier cosine series is

$$
f(x) \sim (-2-3\pi) + \sum_{n=1}^\infty 
\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\dfrac{12(1-(-1)^n)}{\pi n^2}} 
\cdot 
\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\cos(nx)}.
$$

Let $F(x)=5{x}^{2}+2$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=5{x}^{2}+2$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(5{x}^{2}+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[\frac{5{x}^{3}}{3}+2x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{5{\pi }^{3}}{3}+2\pi )-0 \\  & =2(\frac{5{\pi }^{2}}{3}+2).\end{aligned}
$$
